examples.ko: 이번 달 할부금을 아직 못 냈어요.
examples.en: I haven't paid this month's installment yet.
The installment is so big that it's a burden.
The card installment comes out of my account every payday.
I pay the installment on the 25th of every month.

examples.ko: 자동차 할부금을 다 갚으면 좀 여유가 생길 거예요.
examples.en: Once I finish paying off the car installments, I'll have a bit more room.

examples.ko: 할부금 때문에 이번 달에는 여행을 못 가요.
examples.en: Because of the installments, I can't go on a trip this month.

explain: 월세처럼 매달 내는 돈이지만, 물건값을 나눠서 갚는 돈이에요. '내다', '갚다', '빠져나가다'와 자주 같이 써요. 한 번에 내는 '일시불'과 반대로 생각하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: Like monthly rent it is paid every month, but it is money you pay to split the price of something. It often goes with '내다' (to pay), '갚다' (to pay off) and '빠져나가다' (to be withdrawn). It is easy to remember as the opposite of '일시불' (paying all at once).

examples.ko: 이 냉장고는 열두 달로 할부해서 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought this fridge in twelve monthly installments.

examples.ko: 카드로 할부하면 이자가 붙을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pay in installments by card, interest can be added.
I'm paying for the laptop in installments over twelve months.

examples.ko: 한 번에 내기 어려워서 할부하고 싶어요.
examples.en: It's hard to pay all at once, so I want to pay in installments.

examples.ko: 무이자로 할부할 수 있는 카드가 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a card that lets me pay in installments without interest?
I bought my phone in installments last month.

explain: 보통 '할부로 사다', '할부로 결제하다'처럼 '할부로'를 많이 써요. 반대말은 '일시불'이고, 가게에서는 '일시불로 하세요, 할부로 하세요?'라고 물어봐요.
explain_en: People often say '할부로 사다' or '할부로 결제하다' with '할부로'. The opposite is '일시불', and shops ask '일시불로 하세요, 할부로 하세요?' (lump sum or installments?).

en: extra charge; additional charge; premium; surcharge

examples.ko: 밤 열두 시가 넘으면 택시 요금에 할증이 붙어요.
examples.en: After midnight, a surcharge is added to the taxi fare.
The late-night surcharge hours differ by region.
I left early to avoid the surcharge.
Is there a surcharge on the room price in the high season?
This fare includes a surcharge.

examples.ko: 할증 때문에 택시비가 평소보다 훨씬 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Because of the surcharge, the taxi fare was much higher than usual.

explain: 택시 '심야 할증'이나 보험료 이야기에서 가장 많이 들어요. 값을 깎아 주는 '할인'과 반대 방향이에요. '할증이 붙다', '할증이 적용되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: You hear it most in talk about taxi late-night surcharges and insurance premiums. It goes the opposite way from '할인' (discount). Typical phrases are '할증이 붙다' and '할증이 적용되다'.

examples.en: At night, you pay a taxi surcharge separately.
Please tell me in advance how much the surcharge is.
Can I pay the surcharge by card too?
With the surcharge included, it's over 20,000 won.

examples.ko: 할증료 때문에 요금이 생각보다 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The fare was higher than I expected because of the surcharge.
This hotel has a surcharge on weekends.

explain: '할증'이 더 붙는다는 일 자체를 말한다면, '할증료'는 그때 실제로 내는 돈을 말할 때 써요. '할증료를 내다', '할증료가 붙다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서는 '추가 요금'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '할증' is the fact that extra gets added, while '할증료' is the actual money you pay for it. Say '할증료를 내다' or '할증료가 붙다'. In everyday talk people also say '추가 요금' (extra fee).

examples.en: The child broke into a broad smile on getting the present.

examples.ko: 남자는 사진 속에서 청바지를 입고 함박웃음을 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: In the photo, the man is wearing jeans and smiling broadly.
Grandma welcomed me with a big, bright smile.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 엄마 얼굴에 함박웃음이 가득했어요.
examples.en: Mom's face was full of smiles at the news that I passed.
I saw a photo of my friends smiling broadly.
His big smile put me in a good mood too.

explain: '활짝 웃다'처럼 얼굴 전체로 크게 웃는 모습이 그려져요. '함박웃음을 짓다/웃다/터뜨리다'처럼 써요. 소리 내어 크게 웃는 '폭소'와는 달리 환하게 웃는 모습에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: It paints a picture of a smile that lights up the whole face, like '활짝 웃다'. Use it as '함박웃음을 짓다/웃다/터뜨리다'. Unlike '폭소' (a burst of loud laughter), it is closer to a bright, beaming smile.

examples.en: The sugar content of this snack is high.

examples.ko: 제품에 적힌 나트륨 함유량을 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check the sodium content written on the product.
The content differs a little from product to product.
The price differs depending on the vitamin content.

examples.ko: 이 물은 미네랄 함유량이 어느 정도예요?
examples.en: How much mineral content does this water have?
I bought a low-salt soy sauce with reduced content.

explain: 보통 '설탕 함유량', '나트륨 함유량'처럼 앞에 성분 이름을 붙여 써요. 포장지나 뉴스, 건강 이야기에서 자주 보여요. '함유량이 높다/낮다/많다/적다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is usually used with an ingredient in front, as in '설탕 함유량' or '나트륨 함유량'. You often see it on packaging, in the news and in health talk. Say '함유량이 높다/낮다/많다/적다'.

examples.en: Don't rationalize your mistake; apologize first.
That's just rationalizing your laziness.

examples.ko: 자기 합리화가 심한 사람과는 대화하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to talk with someone who rationalizes their own actions a lot.

examples.ko: 회사는 업무 절차 합리화를 추진하고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is pushing to make its work procedures more rational.

examples.ko: 변명처럼 들리는 합리화는 누구나 해 본 적 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has made rationalizations that sound like excuses.

examples.ko: 그 선택을 합리화할 이유를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a reason to justify that choice.

explain: 일상에서는 '자기 합리화'라는 말로 자주 써서, 잘못을 그럴듯한 이유로 덮는 안 좋은 느낌이 있어요. 반면 회사나 제도 이야기에서는 '절차를 합리화하다'처럼 더 효율적으로 바꾼다는 중립적인 뜻으로도 써요. 앞에 오는 말을 보고 구별해요.
explain_en: In daily talk it often appears as '자기 합리화' and has a negative feel of covering a fault with a plausible reason. In talk about companies or systems, as in '절차를 합리화하다', it is neutral and means making something more efficient. Look at the word before it to tell which one is meant.

examples.ko: 자리가 없어서 다른 손님과 합석을 했어요.
examples.en: There were no seats, so I shared a table with another customer.
Sorry, but would it be possible to share a table?

examples.ko: 식당에서 모르는 사람과의 합석은 조금 불편해요.
examples.en: Sharing a table with a stranger at a restaurant is a bit uncomfortable.
If you don't mind sharing a table, please sit here.

examples.ko: 합석으로 앉으면 더 많은 손님이 들어올 수 있어요.
examples.en: If people share tables, more customers can come in.
Thank you for agreeing to share the table.

explain: '합석이 가능할까요?', '합석해도 될까요?'처럼 부탁할 때 많이 들어요. 보통 따로 온 사람들이 한 테이블을 같이 쓸 때 말해요. 식당이나 카페처럼 자리가 모자란 곳에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You hear it a lot when asking, as in '합석이 가능할까요?' or '합석해도 될까요?'. It usually refers to people who came separately sharing one table. It comes up in places like restaurants and cafes when seats are short.

examples.ko: 자리가 없으면 다른 분들과 합석해야 해요.
examples.en: If there are no seats, you have to share a table with other people.
Would it be okay if we sat together?

examples.ko: 처음 보는 사람과 합석하기는 좀 어색해요.
examples.en: Sharing a table with someone I've just met is a bit awkward.
I shared a table with someone I met for the first time at the gathering.

examples.ko: 손님이 많아서 두 팀이 합석하게 됐어요.
examples.en: There were so many customers that two groups ended up sharing a table.
Would you like to join us at our table?

explain: '합석해도 될까요?'처럼 허락을 구할 때 많이 써요. 높이려면 '합석하세요', '합석하시겠어요?'라고 해요. 같은 일행이 아니어도 한 테이블에 앉을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is often used to ask permission, as in '합석해도 될까요?'. To be polite, say '합석하세요' or '합석하시겠어요?'. It is used even when people are not in the same party but sit at one table.

examples.en: It was my first time sharing a taxi, so I was a bit nervous.
I went home late at night by sharing a ride.

examples.ko: 합승을 하면 요금을 나눠 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you share a ride, you can split the fare.
An app that allows ride sharing has come out.
How is the shared-ride fare calculated?
If you agree to share the ride, please press the button.

explain: 택시나 차를 모르는 사람과 같이 탈 때 많이 써요. '합승 요금', '합승 서비스'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙기도 해요. 동사로 말할 때는 '합승하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is often used when you share a taxi or car with people you don't know. Other words can follow it, as in '합승 요금' or '합승 서비스'. As a verb, use '합승하다'.

examples.en: I shared a taxi with my friend and went home.
If we're going the same way, can we share a ride?
Sharing a ride with a stranger is a bit scary.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 옆집 사람과 합승했어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so I shared a ride with my neighbor.
If you share a ride, the taxi fare is cut in half.
Would you like to share a ride with us?

explain: '택시에 합승하다'처럼 '에'를 같이 써요. 높임은 '합승하세요', '합승하실래요?'예요. 같은 방향 사람끼리 요금을 나누려고 할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used with '에', as in '택시에 합승하다'. The polite forms are '합승하세요' and '합승하실래요?'. It is common when people going the same way want to split the fare.

examples.en: This film is a joint work of Korea and France.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 두 가수의 합작품이라서 더 특별해요.
examples.en: That song is a collaboration of two singers, so it's more special.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 여러 건축가의 합작품으로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: This building is known as the joint work of several architects.
The finished cake was a joint effort of the whole family.
For a joint work, the quality is really high.

examples.ko: 합작품은 의견을 맞추는 과정이 힘들 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a joint work, the process of matching opinions can be hard.

explain: 영화·드라마·음악처럼 두 나라나 두 사람 이상이 함께 만든 작품에 써요. 가볍게는 '우리 가족의 합작품'처럼 여럿이 힘을 모아 이룬 결과물에도 써요. '공동 작품'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for works such as films, dramas and music made together by two countries or two or more people. In a lighter way, it also fits results many people made together, like '우리 가족의 합작품'. People sometimes say '공동 작품' instead.

examples.en: The doctor suggested starting anticancer drug treatment.
He had a hard time while receiving the anticancer drugs.
I saw news that a new anticancer drug has been developed.
Anticancer drugs can have side effects.
My father lost his hair because of the anticancer drugs.
They are researching ingredients used as anticancer drugs.

explain: 병원 이야기나 뉴스에서 '항암 치료'와 함께 자주 나와요. 약국에서 쉽게 사는 약이 아니라 병원에서 의사가 정해 주는 약이에요. '항암제를 맞다', '항암제를 쓰다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It often appears with '항암 치료' (chemotherapy) in hospital talk and the news. It is not a drug you easily buy at a pharmacy; a doctor decides it at the hospital. Say '항암제를 맞다' or '항암제를 쓰다'.

examples.en: Sea cucumber makes a crunchy sound when you chew it.
I ordered a plate of sea cucumber at the raw fish restaurant.
I didn't know sea cucumber was this chewy.

examples.ko: 중국 음식점에서 해삼 요리를 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a sea cucumber dish at a Chinese restaurant.
I watched a video of people catching sea cucumbers in the sea.
Do you like a soft texture like sea cucumber?

explain: 횟집이나 중식당 메뉴에서 볼 수 있는 바다 먹거리예요. 모양은 낯설어도 '쫄깃쫄깃', '오독오독' 같은 식감 표현과 같이 많이 말해요. 처음 먹는 사람은 식감 때문에 호불호가 갈려요.
explain_en: It is a seafood item you can see on menus at raw fish restaurants and Chinese restaurants. Even if its look is unfamiliar, people often describe it with texture words like '쫄깃쫄깃' (chewy) and '오독오독' (crunchy). First-timers often like it or dislike it because of the texture.

en: relieving a hangover; eating a soup or having a drink for a hangover

examples.en: Hot soup is the best way to settle your stomach the next day.
People often eat bean sprout soup to settle the stomach.
The hangover soup restaurant had many customers from the morning.

examples.ko: 속이 안 좋을 때는 해장에 좋은 국물이 생각나요.
examples.en: When my stomach feels bad, I think of soup that's good for settling it.

examples.ko: 해장이 필요할 때는 따뜻한 국을 먹어요.
examples.en: When I need to settle my stomach, I eat a warm soup.

examples.ko: 한국 사람들은 해장을 위해 라면도 먹어요.
examples.en: Koreans also eat ramyeon to settle their stomachs.

explain: '해장국', '해장 라면'처럼 뒤에 음식 이름을 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 과음한 다음 날 속을 풀려고 먹는 따뜻한 국물 음식 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 식당 간판에서도 '해장국'이라는 말을 쉽게 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is often followed by a food name, as in '해장국' or '해장 라면'. It comes up in talk about warm, soupy food eaten the day after drinking too much to settle the stomach. You can easily see the word '해장국' on restaurant signs.

en: relieve a hangover; eat a soup or have a drink for a hangover

examples.en: At lunch I settled my stomach with a rice soup.
My stomach burned, so I wondered what to eat to settle it.
I boiled bean sprout soup to settle my stomach.
I went to a nearby rice soup place to settle my stomach.
Eating this broth makes me feel like my stomach is settling.

examples.ko: 해장해야 하니까 오늘은 매운 건 빼 주세요.
examples.en: I need to settle my stomach, so please leave out the spicy stuff today.

explain: '국밥으로 해장하다'처럼 방법을 '(으)로'로 말해요. 많이 마신 다음 날 속을 달래는 상황이라서 보통 아침이나 점심에 써요. 가볍게는 '속을 풀다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: You state the method with '(으)로', as in '국밥으로 해장하다'. It describes calming your stomach the day after heavy drinking, so it is usually used for morning or lunch. A lighter way to say it is '속을 풀다'.

en: finish up; get through; get done

examples.ko: 밀린 숙제를 오늘 안에 다 해치웠어요.
examples.en: I got all my backed-up homework done today.
Let's knock out the urgent work first, then rest.
I'll get the dishes done in no time.

examples.ko: 이 많은 일을 하루에 해치울 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can I get through all this work in one day?
If you get it done quickly, you'll have time in the evening.

examples.ko: 점심을 후다닥 해치워서 회의에 늦지 않았어요.
examples.en: I wolfed down lunch, so I wasn't late for the meeting.

explain: 그냥 '하다'가 아니라 귀찮거나 쌓인 일을 빠르게 끝낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 음식을 빨리 많이 먹을 때도 써요. 그래서 정성을 들여야 하는 일에는 잘 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '하다', it feels like finishing a bothersome or piled-up job quickly. It is also used when eating a lot of food fast. So it does not fit things that need careful effort.

examples.en: Where to bury the nuclear waste is a big problem.
The news covered whether nuclear waste is stored safely.

examples.ko: 핵폐기물 처리 방법을 두고 의견이 갈려요.
examples.en: Opinions are split over how to handle nuclear waste.
I read an article about a nuclear waste storage site.
Nuclear waste can stay dangerous for a long time.
We had a discussion about nuclear waste in class.

explain: 뉴스나 사회·과학 수업에서 보는 말이에요. '처리하다', '보관하다', '매립하다' 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요. '핵폐기물 처리장'처럼 뒤에 장소를 나타내는 말을 붙이기도 해요.
explain_en: This word appears in the news and in social studies or science classes. It often goes with verbs like '처리하다' (to process), '보관하다' (to store) and '매립하다' (to bury). A place word can follow it, as in '핵폐기물 처리장'.

examples.en: New potatoes came out, so I steamed and ate them.
I bought a box of new potatoes at the market.
A stir-fry made with new potatoes is delicious.
New potatoes have thin skin, so they're easy to peel.
My mother sent me new potatoes.
New potatoes taste good with just a sprinkle of salt.

explain: '햇-'은 그해에 처음 나온 것 앞에 붙어서 햇과일, 햇고구마, 햅쌀처럼 써요. 햅쌀은 '햇쌀'이 아니라 '햅쌀'로 쓰니 주의하세요. 오래 두고 먹은 것은 '묵은 감자'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '햇-' is put before things that came out for the first time that year, as in 햇과일, 햇고구마 and 햅쌀. Note that new rice is '햅쌀', not '햇쌀'. Potatoes kept for a long time are called '묵은 감자'.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 햇과일이 시장에 많이 나와요.
examples.en: In autumn, lots of new-season fruit appears in the market.
I bought new-season fruit and sent it to my parents.
The new-season fruit tastes very sweet and fresh.
This shop makes juice from new-season fruit.
New-season fruit is best when eaten in season.
In the morning I have yogurt with new-season fruit.

explain: '햇-'이 붙으면 올해 처음 수확한 것이라는 느낌이 더해져서, 선물할 때도 '햇과일'이라고 하면 신선한 느낌이 나요. '제철 과일'과 가깝지만 '햇과일'은 올해 처음 나왔다는 점에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: When '햇-' is added, it gives the feel of being harvested for the first time this year, so '햇과일' sounds fresh when you give it as a gift. It is close to '제철 과일' (seasonal fruit), but '햇과일' focuses on the fact that it is this year's first harvest.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 아직 햇병아리라서 실수가 많아요.
examples.en: The new employee is still a rookie, so he makes many mistakes.
When it comes to cooking, I'm a complete beginner.
When I was a rookie, my seniors helped me a lot.
I went to the countryside to see the newly hatched chicks at the farm.
Thank you for giving a rookie like me a chance.
He's a rookie reporter, but his questions are sharp.

explain: 원래는 막 깬 병아리인데, 사람에게 쓰면 경험이 거의 없는 초보를 가리켜요. 스스로 낮춰 말할 때는 겸손하게 들리지만, 남에게 쓰면 얕보는 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 비슷한 말은 '초보', '신참'이에요.
explain_en: It originally means a freshly hatched chick, but for people it points to a beginner with almost no experience. Used about yourself it sounds humble, but about someone else it can sound belittling. Similar words are '초보' and '신참'.

examples.ko: 우리가 만난 지 햇수로 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: Counting by calendar years, it's been ten years since we met.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 햇수를 세어 보니 백 년이 넘었어요.
examples.en: When I counted the years, this tree is over a hundred years old.
I've lived in Korea for quite a lot of years.

examples.ko: 햇수는 두 해째지만 사실 일 년 반밖에 안 됐어요.
examples.en: It's the second year by count, but really it's only been a year and a half.
The salary changes depending on the number of years worked.
If you only count the years, I'm the senior.

explain: '햇수로 삼 년'처럼 달력의 해를 센 숫자로 말할 때 많이 써요. 실제로 지난 기간인 '만 삼 년'과는 다를 수 있어요. 비슷하게 달은 '달수', 날은 '날수'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is often used for counting calendar years, as in '햇수로 삼 년'. This can differ from the actual time passed, such as a full three years ('만 삼 년'). In the same way, months are '달수' and days are '날수'.

examples.en: I'm a lucky person to have met good friends.

examples.ko: 복권에 당첨된 그는 모두가 부러워하는 행운아가 됐어요.
examples.en: He won the lottery and became a lucky guy everyone envies.

examples.ko: 이런 가족을 둔 나는 행운아라고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think I'm lucky to have a family like this.

examples.ko: 사고에서 다치지 않은 걸 보면 정말 행운아네요.
examples.en: Seeing that you weren't hurt in the accident, you're really lucky.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 마지막 순간에 골을 넣은 행운아로 불려요.
examples.en: That player is called a lucky guy for scoring in the last moment.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 행운아처럼 보이지만 노력을 많이 했어요.
examples.en: He looks like a lucky guy, but he worked very hard.

explain: 운이 좋은 사람을 부러워하거나 칭찬하는 마음을 담아 말해요. 자기 자신에게 쓰면 '나는 행운아다'처럼 감사한 마음이 담겨요. 일상에서는 '운이 좋은 사람'이라고 풀어서 가볍게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It carries admiration or praise for someone with good luck. About yourself, as in '나는 행운아다', it expresses gratitude. In daily talk people also say '운이 좋은 사람' in a lighter way.

examples.en: Many people are struggling under debt.
I spent my childhood struggling with poverty.
I'm buried in work and struggle every day.

examples.ko: 생활비에 허덕이다 보면 저축은 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: If you're struggling with living costs, you can't even dream of saving.
Prices have gone up, and ordinary people are struggling.
I was chased by a deadline and struggled all night.

explain: '빚에 허덕이다', '일에 허덕이다'처럼 '~에'를 붙여서 힘들게 하는 대상을 말해요. 돈·시간·일이 모자라거나 너무 많아서 쉴 틈 없이 힘든 상황에 써요. 단순히 힘든 하루보다 오래 이어지는 어려움에 어울려요.
explain_en: You add '~에' to name what makes things hard, as in '빚에 허덕이다' or '일에 허덕이다'. It is used when money, time or work is too little or too much and there's no time to rest. It fits a hardship that goes on for a while more than a single tough day.

examples.en: I had no time, so I rushed out of the house in a flustered way.
I got a sudden question and got flustered.
Don't panic; try to do it slowly.
When the child got lost, he started to flounder around.
I got flustered during the presentation and tripped over my words.
Customers are crowding in, so the staff are in a flurry.

explain: 급하거나 당황해서 어쩔 줄 모르고 움직이는 모습에 써요. '허둥지둥'은 같은 느낌의 부사라서 '허둥지둥 뛰어갔어요'처럼 자주 써요. '허둥대다'도 같은 느낌으로 써요.
explain_en: It is used for moving about not knowing what to do because you are rushed or flustered. '허둥지둥' is an adverb with the same feel, as in '허둥지둥 뛰어갔어요'. '허둥대다' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: The athlete lightly jumped over the high hurdle.
Rhythm is important in hurdle races.
I tripped on a hurdle during PE class.
The hurdle to getting a job feels too high.
Passing the exam is the first hurdle.
Try clearing the small hurdles one by one first.

explain: 육상 경기 말고도 '입학 허들', '진입 허들'처럼 넘기 어려운 조건이나 장벽을 비유로 말할 때 써요. 이럴 때는 '허들이 높다/낮다', '허들을 넘다'처럼 말해요. 영어 hurdle에서 온 외래어예요.
explain_en: Beyond track and field, it is used figuratively for a hard condition or barrier, as in '입학 허들' or '진입 허들'. In that sense say '허들이 높다/낮다' or '허들을 넘다'. It is a loanword from English 'hurdle'.

examples.en: They tore down the old wall and built a new one.
The typhoon brought down the wall of the old house.
Please don't knock down the sandcastle.
They say they plan to tear down the old building.

examples.ko: 아이가 쌓은 블록을 동생이 허물어뜨려서 울었어요.
examples.en: His little brother knocked down the blocks he stacked, so he cried.

examples.ko: 편견을 허물어뜨리면 친구가 더 많아질 거예요.
examples.en: If you break down prejudice, you'll have more friends.

explain: '허물다'와 거의 같은 뜻인데 '-뜨리다'가 붙어서 한꺼번에 무너지게 하는 느낌이 더 강해요. 건물뿐 아니라 '벽을 허물다', '편견을 허물다'처럼 마음의 벽에도 써요. 저절로 무너지는 건 '허물어지다'예요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '허물다', but the '-뜨리다' ending gives a stronger feel of bringing something down all at once. It is used not only for buildings but also for mental walls, as in '벽을 허물다' or '편견을 허물다'. Something collapsing by itself is '허물어지다'.

examples.ko: 가게에 갔는데 문을 닫아서 허탕을 쳤어요.
examples.en: I went to the shop but it was closed, so it was a wasted trip.
I waited all day, and it came to nothing again today.
I went fishing but came back empty-handed.

examples.ko: 괜히 갔다가 허탕 칠까 봐 먼저 전화해 봤어요.
examples.en: I called first so I wouldn't make a wasted trip.
It ended up for nothing, and I felt so empty.

examples.ko: 두 시간을 헤맸는데 결국 허탕이 됐어요.
examples.en: I wandered for two hours and it all came to nothing.

explain: '허탕을 치다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요. 찾아가거나 기대했는데 헛걸음만 한 상황에 쓰고, 노력이 아무 결과 없이 끝났을 때도 말해요. 가볍게 투덜거릴 때 '아, 허탕이네' 하고 말해요.
explain_en: The most common pairing is '허탕을 치다'. It is used when you went somewhere or expected something and made a wasted trip, and also when effort ended with no result. When grumbling lightly, people say '아, 허탕이네'.

examples.en: That person exaggerates way too much.
Stop bragging so much.
Everyone laughed when they heard my friend's tall tales.
I knew it was bluster, but I listened with interest.

examples.ko: 허풍은 처음에는 재밌지만 계속 들으면 피곤해요.
examples.en: Boasting is fun at first, but it gets tiring if you keep hearing it.
Be careful not to be fooled by bluster.

explain: '허풍을 떨다/치다'로 많이 써요. 없는 것을 있는 것처럼 크게 부풀려 말할 때 쓰고, 친한 사이에서는 놀리듯 '허풍 좀 그만 떨어'라고도 해요. '거짓말'보다는 가볍게 들리지만 믿음을 잃게 할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '허풍을 떨다/치다'. It is for blowing things up as if you had what you don't, and among close friends people tease with '허풍 좀 그만 떨어'. It sounds lighter than '거짓말' (a lie), but it can still make people stop trusting you.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 허풍쟁이라서 말을 반만 들어요.
examples.en: My uncle is a braggart, so I only half believe him.
He has a reputation as a braggart.
My braggart friend started showing off again.
Nobody wants to be a blowhard.
Everyone calls him a braggart.
Don't talk like a blowhard; just tell the facts.

explain: '-쟁이'가 붙어 그런 버릇이 있는 사람을 놀릴 때 쓰는 말이라서, 친한 사이가 아니면 직접 말하지 않는 게 좋아요. 비슷한 말로 '허풍선이'가 있어요. 없는 일을 지어내기보다 사실을 부풀려 말하는 사람에게 많이 써요.
explain_en: Because '-쟁이' is used to tease someone with such a habit, it is better not to say it directly to anyone you're not close to. A similar word is '허풍선이'. It is often used for someone who inflates the facts rather than makes things up.

examples.en: I ran up the stairs and gasped for breath.

examples.ko: 산 정상에 도착하니 다들 헉헉 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: When we reached the summit, everyone was panting and exhausted.

examples.ko: 마라톤 결승선에 들어온 선수가 헉헉 숨을 골랐어요.
examples.en: The runner who reached the marathon finish line panted to catch his breath.
I ran panting, afraid I'd miss the bus.
I heard heavy panting, and when I turned around it was my friend.

examples.ko: 강아지가 여름에 헉헉 숨을 쉬며 혀를 내밀어요.
examples.en: In summer, the puppy pants with its tongue out.

explain: '헉헉 뛰다', '헉헉 숨을 쉬다'처럼 뒤에 오는 동사를 꾸며요. '헉헉거리다/헉헉대다'로 바꿔 쓸 수도 있어요. 사람뿐 아니라 더운 날의 강아지 숨소리에도 써요.
explain_en: It modifies the verb after it, as in '헉헉 뛰다' or '헉헉 숨을 쉬다'. You can also turn it into '헉헉거리다' or '헉헉대다'. It is used not only for people but also for a dog's breathing on a hot day.

examples.en: My friend who climbed the hill spoke while panting.
Why are you panting like that?
Even while gasping, I ran to the end.

examples.ko: 조금만 걸어도 헉헉거리면 운동을 시작해야 해요.
examples.en: If you pant after a short walk, you need to start exercising.
I was huffing and puffing, but I didn't give up until the finish line.

examples.ko: 헉헉거리지 말고 천천히 숨을 쉬어 봐요.
examples.en: Stop gasping and try breathing slowly.

explain: '헉헉대다'와 거의 같은 말이에요. 달리기나 계단을 오른 뒤 숨이 차서 힘든 모습에 써요. 사람뿐 아니라 강아지처럼 숨을 거칠게 쉬는 동물에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '헉헉대다'. It is used for being out of breath and struggling after running or climbing stairs. It can be used not only for people but also for animals breathing hard, like dogs.

examples.en: The shoes are loose, so it's uncomfortable to walk.
I may have lost weight; my pants feel loose.
I tightened the loose screw with a screwdriver.
The rope is tied too loosely.
The watch I bought yesterday was loose on my wrist.

examples.ko: 헐겁다고 느껴지면 한 사이즈 작은 걸 입어 보세요.
examples.en: If it feels loose, try a size smaller.

explain: 신발·옷·반지처럼 몸에 꼭 맞지 않고 남는 느낌일 때 써요. 반대로 꼭 맞거나 작으면 '꽉 끼다'라고 해요. 나사·줄처럼 단단히 조여 있지 않은 물건에도 쓰고, 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '헐거워요', '헐거운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It is used when shoes, clothes or rings don't fit snugly and feel too roomy. When something fits tightly or is too small, say '꽉 끼다'. It also applies to things not tightened firmly, like screws and ropes, and as a ㅂ-irregular it becomes '헐거워요' and '헐거운'.
